review_text_raw: Good ideas hobbled by bad design and railroading. The stories are interesting, it's exciting to see them unfold and piece together the puzzle. However you can only gather data in a predetermined order, use only the tools the game thinks are necessary, the endless copy-pasting gets boring very quickly (why not autofill information into the relevant field?), and the phone calls, texting are unskippable. This just kills the pacing and makes the mildly interesting core mechanics a chore.

review_text_raw:
I wanted to like this game as it's clear that quite a bit of effort was put into making it, and (at least at the date of this review) the developer is still trying to improve on it.  The graphics are nice and I like this genre of game.  Game play length is decent, you can complete it within 9-10 hours at a leisurely pace.

Having said that, I can't bring myself to recommend it.  The worst part of the game is the writing. Aside from some translation and grammatical errors which I can ignore, the nicest way I can put it is that the writing style is simply not for me. The characters are so incredibly tropey, dramatic and honestly cringey in the way they speak. The twists and turns are juvenile and the themes are simplistic and shallow. The game doesn't say anything you don't already know (i.e. wouldn't it be bad if hackers are able to use your private data on social media for nefarious means? Really makes you think!).

Aside from the writing, the game play is okay though fairly repetitive.  The game does try to keep you engaged with new mini games that pop up, though at least one puzzle right at the end of the game is completely frustrating in a way that makes no sense and when you're under time pressure as well. By that point, I just wanted the game to be finished.

I'm sure there's an audience for this game (maybe younger people?) but it's not for me unfortunately.
